findings.title: Cache status not refreshed after deleting cache
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The disconnect mutation does invalidate it, and that query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. So after a successful delete, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated" and the delete action for data that no longer exists, until a manual reload.

findings.title: Timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The date is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`. The surrounding string is localized through `t()`, but the timestamp ignores the user's locale and time-format preference. Non-US users see month/day ordering and a 12h clock regardless of their settings. Use the user's locale (e.g. `i18n.language`) or the existing dayjs/time-format helpers.

findings.title: Empty-data updateMany adds a write per cache refresh and may be a no-op
findings.body:
`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is called after every cache refresh, which includes every Google webhook notification. That adds an UPDATE across all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential each time.

With empty `data`, Prisma may skip the query entirely or not bump `@updatedAt`, so the stated goal may not even be achieved. The PR notes also say this value isn't displayed anywhere. Remove the call, or set an explicit field if a timestamp is actually needed.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId from all callers
findings.body:
`allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. The function is also re-exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries` as `getConnectedDestinationCalendars`. Any caller that selects only externalId/integration/eventTypeId will now fail type-checking, which includes platform API v2 and other repositories that build this user shape. Only `findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated.

These fields aren't used inside this function, so the type widening looks unnecessary.

findings.title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
findings.body: A plain `Error` is thrown when the credential is not found or not owned by the user. tRPC maps it to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), and the failure is logged as a server error instead of a client authorization/not-found condition. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) instead.

findings.title: Migration warning comment contradicts the SQL
findings.body: The header warns that the required `updatedAt` column was added "without a default value" and that this is "not possible if the table is not empty". The statement actually adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so it is safe on populated tables. The stale auto-generated warning will mislead anyone reviewing migrations and should be removed.

findings.title: BSD-only `sed -i ''` breaks on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is macOS/BSD syntax. On GNU sed (Linux, most CI and dev containers), the `''` is parsed as the sed script and the real expression as a filename, so the env file update fails. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is also resolved relative to the caller's cwd rather than the script location, so running the script from the repo root writes outside the repo.

findings.title: dev:cron depends on tsx which is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script now runs `npx tsx`, but `tsx` isn't listed in devDependencies (`ts-node` still is). npx will download tsx at run time, which needs network access and uses an unpinned version, so the command is non-reproducible and fails offline. Add `tsx` as a devDependency, or keep `ts-node`.

findings.title: No tests for new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
findings.body: The new mutation includes an authorization check: it must only delete cache for credentials owned by the caller. The new repository aggregation feeds the UI. Neither has unit tests, so regressions in the ownership check or the credential-to-status mapping would go unnoticed.
